doc.title: Ametria Dock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 4, 2019

chapter: Church upbringing and singing on the spot
title: Growing up in a Pentecostal pastor's household full of Gospel
summary: Her father was a Pentecostal pastor and B3 player; Gospel was the only music at home, in a large musical extended family.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Okay. Let me ask you about your upbringing a little bit. Almost as an aside yesterday you had mentioned the Pentecostal church experience, and that you listened to secular music sort of on the sly?

So my dad was the pastor, a Pentecostal pastor. And in our household the only thing that was an option was Gospel music. And so, and that was in my early years growing up. It was just — that Gospel music and my dad was a musician so we had a lot of live Gospel — and I’ve been saying this word all the time because it’s the word that we say, it’s just like vibe sessions, or worship sessions, where it was just live music and voices. And so that was a thing in my house, and my family, my grandparents’ homes, my aunts and my uncles. My dad had ten brothers and sisters so we had a really big family. Everyone in the family was musically inclined. Everyone. My aunts played keys and guitar and my father © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
played the B3 and piano, and so I came from that kind of upbringing in the Pentecostal church. Gospel was what was central in our house.
